gap: No result ChatGPT got states that OWC's own Express 1M2 manual says it runs at only USB 10Gb/s on Thunderbolt 3 hosts. Sabrent rates its fan-cooled EC-U4TN at 2,700 MB/s over Thunderbolt, against 990 MB/s in OWC's table for a 10Gb/s link. So on an Intel Thunderbolt 3 Mac or PC, ChatGPT's quiet fanless pick is about a third as fast as a fan model before any throttling starts.
standout_why: I compared against itechguides.com (cited), soldermag.com (rank 5, not cited), owc.com/solutions/express-1m2 (cited) and our current page. The owc.com product page says the 1M2 'Works with … Thunderbolt 3' but its speed table has no Thunderbolt 3 row. Itechguides calls the 1M2 'a documented option for compatible Thunderbolt 3 Mac systems' and only adds that 'Thunderbolt 3 behavior varies'. Soldermag only says some ports 'silently fall back to slower modes'. Our page has no host-compatibility column at all. The Tom's Hardware page came back empty, so I could not check it. None of them state the 10Gb/s limit on Thunderbolt 3 or the heatsink-SSD exclusion in OWC's manual.
decides: This settles the pick for shoppers whose host is Thunderbolt 3 (Intel Mac or older PC): avoid the OWC Express 1M2, which OWC caps at USB 10Gb/s there. Prefer an enclosure whose maker states a Thunderbolt speed: Sabrent EC-U4TN says 2,700 MB/s over Thunderbolt and has a fan. It confirms the existing picks for Apple silicon and USB4/TB4 PCs (OWC: 3,189 MB/s on Apple silicon, 3,836 MB/s on a PC). Two caveats for every pick: use the 40Gbps cable in the box, and don't use an SSD with a heatsink in the 1M2.

findings.label: Speed on Thunderbolt 3 hosts
findings.note: Exact wording, said twice (including §3.3): 'hosts with Thunderbolt 3 ports will experience limited performance up to USB 10Gb/s.' OWC's product page gives 990 MB/s for a 10Gb/s USB-C link, so expect that ceiling on Thunderbolt 3.

findings.label: SSD exclusions
findings.value: NVMe SSDs with a heatsink are not supported; NVMe 2230/2242/2280 only, single- or double-sided; some high-power SSDs may need more power than the enclosure supplies
findings.note: Quotes: 'NVMe SSDs with a heatsink will not fit and are not supported.' 'Select high power-draw NVMe SSDs may require more power than provided by the OWC Express 1M2.' 2260 is not listed.

findings.label: Host exclusions
findings.value: Does not mount as the third bus-powered device on some Macs; not compatible with the PS5's front USB-C or USB-A ports
findings.note: From the manual's notes section. Operating temperature is rated 5–35 °C.

findings.label: Speed by host (maker table)
findings.value: Apple silicon M1–M5 over USB4: 3,189 MB/s; PC USB4 or Thunderbolt 4 port: 3,836 MB/s; 10Gb/s USB-C port (iPad, Mac or PC): 990 MB/s
findings.source_title: OWC Express 1M2: Portable USB4 NVMe M.2 SSD Solution
findings.note: The 3,836 MB/s figure is CrystalDiskMark with a 2 TB Aura Ultra IV in an Alienware x14 R2 (footnote 1). The page says it 'Works with … Thunderbolt 3' but has no Thunderbolt 3 row. In the box: 0.3 m (12 in) 40Gb/s cable. Needs a PCIe Gen 3 or later SSD. Warranty: 2 years for the enclosure alone.

findings.label: Speed by host (maker)
findings.value: Up to 3,900 MB/s on USB4, 2,700 MB/s on Thunderbolt, 1,000 MB/s on USB 3.2; takes 2230/2242/2260/2280; has a fan; $89.99
findings.source_title: Sabrent USB4 M.2 PCIe NVMe SSD Enclosure (EC-U4TN)
findings.note: Read through storecheck.py from the store's product data; price is sabrent.com's on 2026-11-08. Sabrent writes 'Thunderbolt' without a version. Since USB4 and TB4 hosts are covered by the 3,900 figure, 2,700 MB/s most likely means Thunderbolt 3, but the page does not say so. The full page returned HTTP 429, so I could not read the FAQ or exclusions.

findings.label: Cable dependency
findings.value: Older USB-C cables gave '10Gbps-like performance'; use the cables in the box (USB-C to USB-C and USB-A to USB-C)
findings.source_title: PCWorld: UGREEN CM642 SSD enclosure review (Jon L. Jacobi, 2025-02-11)
findings.note: Jacobi: 'Be sure to use these rather than older Type-C cables to ensure 40Gbps performance.' He says USB4 runs at 40Gbps on Apple hardware but did not test a Thunderbolt 3 host. He reports the enclosure takes any 2230–2280 NVMe SSD of any capacity, tested with an 8 TB WD SN850X, and saw no thermal issues on a 450 GB write. Price then: $109.99 on Amazon.

findings.label: What the cited rival says about Thunderbolt 3
findings.value: Calls the Express 1M2 'a documented option for compatible Thunderbolt 3 Mac systems'; gives no Thunderbolt 3 speed
findings.source_title: Recommend Me a USB4/TB4/5 NVMe Enclosure: Best Picks (itechguides)
findings.note: Read to compare against. It also says 'Thunderbolt 3 behavior varies across platforms' but never mentions the 10Gb/s limit OWC's manual states.
